memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'For seven days present food offerings to the LORD, and on the eighth
day hold a sacred assembly and present a food offering to the LORD. It
is the closing special assembly; do no regular work'"
- Lev 23:36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Seven days of offerings, and then one more gathering on the eighth day.
A closing assembly. One final coming together before everyone returned
home.

There is something fitting about an ending that is itself an act of
worship. Israel's year did not simply trail off; it closed in God's
presence.

Dear reader, it was almost certainly on this festival that Jesus stood
in the temple courts and cried out, "Let anyone who is thirsty come to
me and drink" (John 7:37). During Tabernacles, priests poured out water
drawn from the pool of Siloam in a daily ceremony. And on the last and
greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and offered Himself as the
true source of living water.

What a moment. Centuries of ritual, and the One it pointed to standing
right there, inviting people to come.

That invitation still stands. It is not for the qualified, the tidy or
the impressive. It is for the thirsty.

However your week has gone, however dry your soul feels, the invitation
has not been withdrawn. Come to Him and drink.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I genuinely thirsty for God, or have I settled for something
   lesser?
2. What "wells" have I been drinking from that never satisfy?
3. How do I close my days and seasons - in God's presence or in a rush?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, I am thirsty and only You can satisfy. I come to You today
and ask You to fill me with Your living water. Amen.
